name: Can I use a bathroom expansion to create a shower-only layout?

mainEntity.name: Is it worth removing the tub and making the expanded bathroom a shower-only space?
mainEntity.text: Is it worth removing the tub and making the expanded bathroom a shower-only space?

acceptedAnswer.text: A shower-only layout is often a smart choice during a bathroom expansion, especially when the goal is to make the room feel more open. Removing a tub can free up valuable floor area for a larger shower, better vanity placement, or easier circulation. It also simplifies cleaning and can make the bathroom feel more modern. For primary suites, a well-designed shower-only room can work very well if the household does not rely on a tub. The main caution is resale: some buyers still expect at least one tub in the home, especially in family-oriented neighborhoods. The best strategy is to think about the entire property, not just one bathroom. If another bathtub remains elsewhere in the house, converting the expanded bathroom to shower-only is often practical. The design should also include proper waterproofing, splash control, and enough drying space so the room stays comfortable and easy to maintain.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, converting to a shower-only layout is a common way to make an expanded bathroom feel larger and more functional. It frees up floor space, simplifies cleaning, and can improve accessibility, but it may affect resale preferences in some homes.
